entry.title: The Rhetoric Student
entry.summary: A student of communication and argument who wants Aristotle's classical text made navigable and glossed for a modern reader.
entry.content:
This reader is new to Aristotle’s Rhetoric and approaches it as a text to be studied, not skimmed. They may be encountering classical rhetorical theory for the first time as part of a course in communication, argumentation, or classics, or they may be reading independently to understand where later persuasion theory comes from.

What they need most is a version of the text that does not assume prior familiarity: unfamiliar terms glossed in place, footnotes that read as part of the argument rather than as scholarly clutter, and enough structural signposting (book, chapter, section) to keep their bearings across a long, dense work. They are patient with the original argument’s pace, but impatient with anything that makes the text harder to follow than the ideas already are.

They measure a converted showcase page as successful when they can read a chapter start to finish, resolve every unfamiliar term without leaving the page, and come away able to summarise the chapter’s argument in their own words.
